newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds and the rand put on another strong showing on Wednesday, buoyed by worldwide enthusiasm for bonds in the wake of benign U.S. December inflation figures and improving local sentiment.
Yields on the benchmark R150 government bond traded down to their lowest levels since late October before retracing slightly to show a net fall on the day of 15 basis points.
The rand held up well against a rampant dollar and was significantly firmer against the British pound and the mark.

Dealers said President Nelson Mandela's stern rebuttal of the U.S. after Washington criticised a proposed arms sale to Syria took the shine off bonds in the afternoon, but sentiment remained fundamentally positive.

"There is risk foreigners will take fright -- although I think it's unjustified -- and we need the foreign exchange," commented Graham Parker, general manager of Infinity Asset Management in Cape Town.
News that the daily money market shortage fell back to 9.765 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.370 billion on Monday also helped.

Although three-month NCD rates remained unchanged, traders said there was a growing belief that liquidity at the short end of the yield curve would soon improve, creating more scope for yields at the long end to come down.

Laurence Rosenberg, director of the bond division at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak, said bonds had got off to a strong start following good after-hours buying by foreigners on Tuesday and the outlook remained positive.
"We're in a fairly strong bull trend which should continue for a while," he said.

Other dealers said there was growing confidence that the rand could stabilise in the medium term which, together with a consolidating economy, was painting a more encouraging picture for bond investors.

Tuesday's prediction by the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (NAAMSA) that new car sales would fall to 242,000 in 1997 from 249,884 in 1996 had highlighted the looming economic slowdown, they added.
The World Bank also leant the market a helping hand, coming in as the latest issuer to raise funds in Eurorands with a 200 million rand issue.

Currency traders said the rand had firmed significantly against its currency basket -- though the impact on the dollar rate was muted by the strength of the greenback -- helped by inflows on the back of offshore bond buying.

"A lot of it is bond-related, we haven't seen many corporates in at all. The market's got potential to get just below 4.65 (against the dollar) but I don't see it much below there unless the bonds carry on down to the 15.35-15.40 area," said one forex dealer.

The rand finished at 4.6550/6600 on the dollar from Tuesday's 4.6690/6740. Against the crosses, it was last trading at 7.7781/7912 on sterling from 7.8017/57 while on the mark it was at 0.3425/3429 from 0.3405/10.
Leading banks edged down their 90-day BA rates to between 16.60 and 16.85 percent from 16.65-16.85 percent but three-month NCD rates were unchanged at between 17.30 and 17.50 percent.
At the long end of the market the R150 bond was yielding 15.62 percent from 15.77 at 1400 GMT Tuesday.

Foreigners bought a net 286.21 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 80.76 million rands on Monday, the Bond Exchange said. Nominal cumulative turnover was 7.11 billion rand from 4.29 billion.
